gate._phase_note: EWSR1 exon 7 ends 1 nt past a codon boundary, so residue 265 is SPLIT across the splice junction. That is a normal exon phase and is reported, not corrected: the PROTEIN-level junction the gate asserts is EWSR1 kept to residue 264, and how the split codon is completed depends on the acceptor exon's own 5' phase.
gate._what_a_refusal_means: the exon structure this run read does not produce the corrected junction; NOTHING downstream may be emitted, because an inventory of the wrong object is worse than no inventory

breakpoints._filter: the declared windows only. Whether a given chimera is the PATIENT's chimera is not decidable from exon structure and is not decided here.

the_sentence: Every structure in this work is an isolated NR4A3 ligand-binding-domain construct (NR4A3 373-626); the EWSR1::NR4A3 fusion protein that defines extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma additionally contains NR4A3 residues 1-372 and, at the canonical exon-derived junction, EWSR1 residues 1-264, so 30 reactive residues — including the NR4A3-unique cysteine C166 — lie outside every structure reported here and outside the reach of every geometric statement made about them.  (NR4A3-unique among those: C166, K178.)  The patient-level breakpoint is not pinned; across every breakpoint the declared windows allow that retains the DNA-binding domain, 30 of the 45 reactive residues enumerated are invariant and 15 are breakpoint-dependent — and every breakpoint-dependent residue is on the EWSR1 side, because the DNA-binding-domain requirement pins the NR4A3 resume and only the EWSR1 cut moves.
